title: Generative Artificial Intelligence-Guided User Studies: An Application for Air Taxi Services
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether generative AI can support early-stage user studies by rapidly creating virtual experimental scenarios, reducing the cost, time, and safety burdens of conventional prototyping. The authors frame the problem in human-computer interaction and transportation design: real-world user testing of emerging technologies such as air taxis is difficult because physical prototypes are immature, expensive to build, and may raise safety concerns during early iteration.

The proposed approach uses OpenAI GPT-4 to generate prompts, pain points, user needs, design requirements, mockups, and storyboard content for an air-taxi journey. AI image and video generators (Midjourney and Runway) were then used to visualize these materials into a virtual experimental scenario. The resulting air-taxi journey was presented to 72 adult participants in an online questionnaire, and their pre/post attitudes toward taking air taxis and their satisfaction with the experience were measured using Likert-scale items.

The study found that viewing the AI-generated journey significantly improved participants’ willingness to take an air taxi and that overall satisfaction was moderate to high. Effects varied by subgroup: education level significantly influenced attitude change, and gender significantly influenced satisfaction, with females reporting lower satisfaction than males. Age and employment status did not show significant differences. The authors conclude that generative AI can help design virtual user-study scenarios for early-stage technology development, but the method should be refined to better simulate real participant responses and to account for demographic differences in attitudes and satisfaction.
quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical user study with pre/post measures and subgroup analyses, but it is not an educational intervention study and lacks randomization/control conditions relevant to K-12 evidence standards. The design is closer to an HCI mixed-methods evaluation than a rigorous causal study in education.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper shows a moderate positive attitudinal shift in a non-educational setting, but the effect is on user acceptance of air taxis rather than learning outcomes. There is no direct educational impact, so the relevance to the requested education-focused taxonomy is limited.

interventions.use_case: LLM-guided user-study design for an air-taxi journey, including prompt-based generation of pain points, user needs, design requirements, mockups, and storyboards, then visualized with AI image/video generators for evaluation.

GPT-4 used as a generative assistant to produce design-thinking outputs (empathize, define, ideate, prototype) and simulate participant responses; not tutoring students, but a conversational AI used to support iterative design and evaluation.

finding.finding_summary: Across 72 participants, viewing the AI-generated air-taxi journey improved willingness/attitudes toward taking an air taxi from M=3.46 pre to M=3.89 post, with a significant paired t-test (t=-3.326, p=0.001). The paper interprets this as generative AI improving acceptance and satisfaction with the simulated experience.
finding.measure: Attitude toward taking an air taxi before vs after viewing the ATJ video/questionnaire

finding.finding_summary: Attitude change differed significantly by education level (F=3.733, p=0.008), with larger gains among lower-education participants and little change among the highest-education group. No significant differences were found by gender, age, or employment status for attitude change (all p>0.05), though all groups trended positive.
finding.measure: Change in willingness/attitude toward taking an air taxi across demographic subgroups

finding.finding_summary: Participants reported high satisfaction with the AI-generated air-taxi journey overall (M=3.78, SD=0.77). Satisfaction differed significantly by gender (t=2.508, p=0.014), with males more satisfied than females, while education, age, and employment status showed no statistically significant differences.
finding.measure: Satisfaction with the simulated air-taxi journey (ATJ)
